final_recommendation: The room converged on a concrete, operationalized risk framework: a single master Policy-to-Supply-Chain Risk Map delivered Friday 1 PM, naming RVC failures, month-16 trade-facility restrictions, month-14-16 insolvency cliffs, nearshoring capex per supplier, production-line exposure by platform, and policy-uncertainty layers—all priced into trade-credit and political-risk underwriting.
minority_objections: Auto strategy initially questioned whether the capex/runway template would break for the 30-40 tier-2/3 suppliers, but this was resolved by supplier's three-way bucketing (forced relocators, phased candidates, triage cases)
key_conflicts: Tension over whether to run full RVC audits on all 40-50 suppliers versus staged approach—resolved by supplier committing to full audits starting immediately
Disagreement on whether RVC failures trigger immediate penalties or coast until month-16 exemption expiry—resolved by compliance lawyer clarifying month-16 cliff as the hard trigger
Conflict over whether nearshoring incentive would be a dollar figure or methodology—resolved by consultant committing to hard capex numbers per supplier
key_concessions: Supplier conceded to running full RVC audits on all 40-50 suppliers immediately (not staged), delivering preliminary fail list end-of-week
CFO conceded to consolidating all risk layers into single master document by Friday 1 PM with real-time model-line specificity
Trade-credit underwriter conceded to pricing triage bucket at month-14-16 insolvency cliff based on working-capital runway, not uniform default rate
Compliance lawyer conceded that retroactive application of stricter labor definitions is not standard—exemptions lock unless circumstances change materially
red_lines: CFO's non-negotiable: single master map delivered Friday morning naming all compliance triggers, pricing gates, and production-line exposure
Compliance lawyer's red line: RVC failures triggering immediate trade-facility loss at month-16 must be binary and named today, separate from cure eligibility
Supplier's red line: front-load 8-10 audits by month-17 to lock status under current rules before USMCA review tightens definitions
Political-risk insurer's red line: month-18 audit date triggers immediate coverage loss with no grace period
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Business-interruption exposure from production halts (e.g., Gen 5 sedan six-week halt) was flagged but not priced into a concrete BI insurance variable
Contingent business interruption from tier-2/3 supplier collapse during forced-relocator requalification was identified but not operationalized into CBI coverage
Labor-cost pressure from wage-floor requirements was implicit in RVC compliance burden but never developed as a separate underwriting variable
downstream_risk_variables: Month-16 trade-facility restriction trigger (binary flag per supplier)
Month-14-16 insolvency cliff timeline per triage-bucket supplier
Nearshoring capex per forced relocator (hard dollar figure)
Production-line exposure by platform (BOM line-item mapping to supplier requalification timelines)
Working-capital runway post-capex (months of runway flagged per supplier)
Logistics viability for 18-month nearshoring (binary flag: feasible vs. exit risk)
uncertainty_notes: The room did not resolve: (1) exact dollar thresholds distinguishing minimum-nearshoring-incentive tier from no-incentive-viable suppliers, (2) whether USMCA review enforcement will tighten labor definitions or trigger retroactive audits (priced on assumption), (3) which specific RVC failures get 30/60-day cure windows versus immediate hard-cliff treatment (CFO tasked to lock this down 'today' but no answer recorded in transcript), (4) how business-interruption exposure from production halts translates into BI/CBI insurance pricing.

marker_evidence.rules_of_origin_burden: Fully operationalized: RVC failures named per supplier, month-16 cliff trigger, immediate trade-facility restrictions, retroactive penalties, front-loaded audits by month-17—all priced into Friday master map.
marker_evidence.labor_cost_pressure: Implicit in RVC labor-content compliance but never developed into a separate cost variable or wage-floor underwriting factor.
marker_evidence.supplier_relocation_pressure: Fully operationalized: three-way bucketing (forced relocators, phased candidates, triage cases), nearshoring capex per supplier (hard dollar figures), logistics viability flags, backup-loss timing mapped to requalification dates.
marker_evidence.nearshoring_incentive: Fully operationalized: hard dollar capex figures per supplier, minimum-nearshoring-incentive tier added to Friday map, binary viability flags (feasible vs. exit risk), tied to production-line exposure.
marker_evidence.trade_credit_stress: Fully operationalized: month-14-16 insolvency cliff per supplier, working-capital runway post-capex (months flagged), trade-facility restrictions at month-16, receivables risk priced into underwriting, triage bucket default rates differentiated.
marker_evidence.political_risk_score: Well-specified but not fully priced: month-18 review enforcement stance (stricter labor definitions, retroactive audits) developed into policy-uncertainty column on master map, but priced 'on assumption' not concrete triggers; month-18 coverage-loss gate is concrete.
marker_evidence.business_interruption_exposure: Identified but not operationalized: Gen 5 sedan six-week production halt flagged, supply collapse during requalification noted, but no BI/CBI insurance pricing, no named triggers or coverage gates.
marker_evidence.consulting_actionability: Fully operationalized: three-column action map (nearshoring viability, phased requalification, exit risks), dollar figures per supplier, logistics viability checks on rolling basis, model-line exposure by BOM, single master doc consolidating all layers—client-executable action plan.
